questions.prompt: Which subtopic is explicitly listed under “Numeric and Mathematical Operations” in the attached Classic ASP curriculum?

questions.prompt: When applying “Numeric and Mathematical Operations” in a legacy Classic ASP application, which approach is strongest?
options: Make the runtime assumptions explicit and test normal, invalid, and boundary values.
Assume every value from a browser is trustworthy.
Enable detailed errors for all public visitors.
Change several settings at once and infer which one fixed the issue.
questions.answer_key: Make the runtime assumptions explicit and test normal, invalid, and boundary values.
questions.explanation: This approach keeps numeric and mathematical operations testable and respects Classic ASP/IIS runtime boundaries. The exact IIS, provider, or component behavior must be checked in the target test environment.

questions.prompt: Before marking work on “Numeric and Mathematical Operations” ready for review, what evidence should be recorded?
options: Claim the production deployment passed without running it.
Delete diagnostic evidence before recording the outcome.
Treat a successful happy-path test as proof of all security properties.
Document the observed result, tool/runtime version, and one meaningful failure or edge case.
questions.answer_key: Document the observed result, tool/runtime version, and one meaningful failure or edge case.
questions.explanation: Good maintenance evidence includes the expected and observed result, relevant version/runtime assumptions, and a boundary or failure test. Never claim an execution/deployment test that was not run.
